name: Secretary of the Interior's order of July 3, 1875 fixing the 1,000-acre Moapa River Reservation
citation: Order of the Secretary of the Interior, July 3, 1875, under the Act of March 3, 1875 (Royce cession 577)
nations: Moapa Band of Paiute Indians (Southern Paiute)
promises: Not a treaty: the Secretary of the Interior's approval of the boundaries of the 1,000 acres that the Act of March 3, 1875 allowed the Southern Paiute to keep. Royce says this tract constitutes the present Moapa reservation (cession 577).
Everything else in the reservations of 1873 and 1874 was released by this selection.

breaches.what: By approving a 1,000-acre selection under the 1875 Act, the Secretary of the Interior completed the reduction of the Moapa River Reservation set apart by the orders of 1873 and 1874; the rest returned to the public domain.
breaches.whoFoundIt: Order of the Secretary of the Interior of July 3, 1875, as recorded in Royce's schedule (Bureau of American Ethnology, 1899)

source.title: Royce, Schedule of Indian Land Cessions, 1874 entries (Moapa reserve)
source.publisher: Bureau of American Ethnology, 18th Annual Report, part 2 (Royce, Indian Land Cessions, 1899), Internet Archive

breaches.what: The Moapa Band's general counsel wrote that the February 12, 1874 order expanded the reservation to well over 2,000,000 acres, that Congress cut it to 1,000 acres in an appropriations rider, and that 99.5% of the reservation was lost when the Secretary made the 1,000-acre selection on July 3, 1875.
breaches.whoFoundIt: Ziontz, Chestnut, Varnell, Berley & Slonim, general counsel to the Moapa Band of Paiutes, letter to the US EPA

source.title: Letter of Ziontz, Chestnut, Varnell, Berley & Slonim, general counsel to the Moapa Band of Paiutes, to the US EPA (May 18, 2004)

breaches.quote: 99.5% of the Reservation was lost to the Tribe at the stroke of a pen

breaches.what: The Southern Paiute claims were settled by compromise before the Indian Claims Commission, which entered a final judgment for the Southern Paiute Nation of $7,253,165.19 under a stipulation of the parties, on behalf of the Southern Paiute bands named in the petitions and the Las Vegas Band. A compromise is not a finding of breach.
breaches.whoFoundIt: Indian Claims Commission, Southern Paiute Nation v. United States, Dockets 88, 330 and 330-A, final judgment on a compromise settlement

source.title: Southern Paiute Nation v. United States, Dockets 88, 330 and 330-A, Final Judgment (January 18, 1965)
source.publisher: Oklahoma State University Library, Indian Claims Commission Decisions

compensation: No payment for the 1875 reduction was found. The Southern Paiute claims were settled by compromise for $7,253,165.19 (Indian Claims Commission, January 18, 1965).
today: Congress restored land to the Moapa reservation by Public Law 96-491, signed on December 2, 1980; President Carter's signing statement gives approximately 70,500 acres, and the Band's counsel gives 70,565 acres and a present reservation of about 72,000 acres (letter of May 18, 2004).

nationVoice.summary: Through its general counsel, the Band describes the 1875 reduction as the loss of 99.5% of its reservation, and says the 1980 restoration of about 70,565 acres was meant to redress that loss in part and give it land for development.

openQuestions: Royce cession 577, attached to this id, is the 1,000 acres the Band kept, not the land taken; the map may show the kept land under a 'broken' label. Jordan may prefer the map to explain that.

Audit 2026-11-08: the Statutes at Large were opened (Library of Congress scan of the 43rd Congress, PDF page 475). The reduction is in the Indian appropriation act of March 3, 1875, ch. 132, at 18 Stat. 445, under Nevada; the Band's counsel's citation of 18 Stat. 475 is a misprint.
Audit 2026-11-08: removed the sentence on Paiute consent from the breach; no source opened says whether consent was or was not sought.

plain.promised: Not a treaty: the Secretary of the Interior's approval of the 1,000 acres the 1875 Act let the Southern Paiute keep. Royce says this tract is the present Moapa reservation.
plain.happened: This selection completed the cut of the Moapa River Reservation set apart in 1873 and 1874, and the rest returned to the public domain. The Moapa Band's counsel says 99.5% of the reservation was lost.
plain.today: No payment for the 1875 cut was found; Southern Paiute claims were settled by compromise for $7,253,165.19 in 1965. In 1980 Congress restored approximately 70,500 acres to the Moapa reservation.
